title: Motherboard failure - power rail
shortDescription: Single amber LED blink indicates motherboard / system board fault.
fullDescription:
Dell laptops use blink-coded power LED diagnostics. A single amber blink (sometimes followed by white) signals that the motherboard is not delivering proper voltage on one of the primary power rails.

This is rarely user-fixable and indicates a hardware fault on the system board. Replacement is usually the only option.

fixSteps.title: Drain residual power
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect AC and battery, hold power button 30 seconds, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect peripherals
fixSteps.instruction: Remove RAM, SSD, and battery. Try booting on AC only with each component reseated one at a time.

fixSteps.title: Replace motherboard
fixSteps.instruction: If pattern persists with all components removed, motherboard replacement is required.

whenToCallPro: If reseating components doesn't help, professional service is needed.

faq.a: Often costs more than the laptop is worth on older models.

title: CPU failure
shortDescription: Two amber blinks indicate CPU not detected or failed.
fullDescription:
Two amber LED blinks on a Dell laptop indicate the BIOS cannot initialize the CPU. The processor may be physically damaged, improperly seated (on rare desktop-replacement units), or the motherboard's CPU socket has failed.

In most laptops the CPU is BGA-soldered, so any CPU failure means motherboard replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, hold power button 30 seconds, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Heat-gun reflow (last resort)
fixSteps.instruction: On older laptops, professional BGA reflow may temporarily restore function — short-term fix only.

whenToCallPro: Always — CPU failures are not user-fixable on laptops.

title: Motherboard / chipset failure
shortDescription: Three amber blinks indicate chipset or memory hub failure.
fullDescription: Three amber LED blinks point to a chipset or memory controller failure on the motherboard. On some XPS and Latitude models, this also relates to BIOS corruption that can be resolved via BIOS recovery.

fixSteps.title: BIOS recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Ctrl+Esc while plugging in AC adapter to trigger Dell BIOS recovery from USB.

fixSteps.title: Replace motherboard
fixSteps.instruction: If recovery fails, system board replacement required.

faq.a: No, it only updates BIOS firmware.

title: RAM failure
fullDescription: Four amber blinks indicate the BIOS cannot initialize RAM. Either no DIMM is detected, the modules have failed, or the slot itself is damaged.

fixSteps.title: Reseat RAM
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove battery, open RAM compartment, reseat both modules firmly.

fixSteps.title: Test single sticks
fixSteps.instruction: Boot with one stick at a time in slot A to identify a failed module.

fixSteps.title: Replace RAM
fixSteps.instruction: Install new SO-DIMMs of correct DDR generation and speed.

whenToCallPro: If RAM is soldered (XPS 13 newer models) — motherboard service needed.

title: CMOS battery failure
shortDescription: RTC / CMOS coin cell battery dead or disconnected.
fullDescription: Five amber blinks indicate the RTC (Real Time Clock) battery — the small CR2032 coin cell — has failed or its cable is disconnected. BIOS cannot maintain time, settings, or some Latitude models will refuse to POST entirely.

fixSteps.title: Replace coin battery
fixSteps.instruction: Open laptop bottom cover, locate CR2032 cell (often wired with a small connector), unplug, install new cell.

fixSteps.title: Reset BIOS to defaults
fixSteps.instruction: Reboot, enter BIOS, load defaults, set time/date.

whenToCallPro: If you can't open the laptop yourself.
videoSearchQuery: Dell laptop 5 amber blinks CMOS battery replace

faq.q: Why is the coin cell so hard to reach?
faq.a: Modern slim Dells bury it under the motherboard.

title: Video card / GPU failure
fullDescription: Six amber blinks signal a video card / GPU failure during POST. Affects laptops with discrete GPUs (NVIDIA / AMD). On integrated-GPU systems, it usually indicates BGA solder failure of the CPU package.

fixSteps.title: Try external monitor
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to external display via HDMI to confirm the issue is GPU not the panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace motherboard
fixSteps.instruction: GPU is BGA — replacement requires motherboard swap or board-level repair.

videoSearchQuery: Dell laptop 6 amber blinks GPU failure

title: CPU exception / failure
fullDescription: Seven amber blinks indicate a CPU runtime fault — the processor passed initial detection but failed BIOS-level testing. Usually means CPU damage from overheating or motherboard fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset and test
fixSteps.instruction: Drain power, try with minimum components.

title: LCD / display failure
shortDescription: BIOS cannot communicate with LCD panel.
fullDescription: Eight amber blinks point to a display-related fault — broken LCD cable, failed LVDS/eDP controller, or damaged panel itself.

fixSteps.title: Reseat LCD cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the screen bezel, reseat the eDP cable on the motherboard side.

fixSteps.title: Replace cable
fixSteps.instruction: Order matching eDP cable for your model.

fixSteps.title: Replace panel
fixSteps.instruction: Order matching LCD panel — check resolution and connector.

videoSearchQuery: Dell 8 amber blinks LCD error fix

faq.a: External display uses HDMI/USB-C, bypassing the internal eDP path.

title: BIOS / firmware update failed
shortDescription: BIOS update was interrupted or corrupted.
fullDescription: Error 0300 appears after a failed BIOS update — power loss during flash, wrong file, or interrupted process. Dell laptops support BIOS recovery via Ctrl+Esc method.

fixSteps.title: BIOS recovery via USB
fixSteps.instruction: Format USB to FAT32, copy BIOS_IMG.rcv from Dell support, plug USB, hold Ctrl+Esc while plugging in adapter.

alternativeCodes: AC adapter type cannot be determined
title: Plugged in, not charging
shortDescription: Battery refuses to charge despite AC connected.
fullDescription: Common Dell issue where Windows shows 'Plugged in, not charging' or BIOS reports 'AC adapter type cannot be determined'. The 1-wire ID inside the Dell adapter cable failed, or aftermarket adapter is in use.

causes.cause: Frayed adapter cable / broken ID wire

fixSteps.title: Use OEM Dell adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace with original Dell adapter rated for your laptop wattage.

fixSteps.title: Replace DC jack
fixSteps.instruction: If pin is loose, replace DC-in cable.

whenToCallPro: If DC jack is soldered to the motherboard.

title: Keyboard not responding
shortDescription: Some or all keys stop working.
fullDescription: Dell laptops often develop keyboard issues — sticky keys, dead rows, or fully unresponsive keyboards — typically from spills, ribbon cable wear, or worn keyboard membrane.

fixSteps.title: Test in BIOS
fixSteps.instruction: If keys work in BIOS but not Windows, it's a software issue — reinstall keyboard driver.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open palmrest assembly, reseat keyboard ribbon connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace keyboard
fixSteps.instruction: Install new keyboard assembly matching your model and layout.

whenToCallPro: On XPS where keyboard is part of palmrest assembly with delicate ribbon connectors.

faq.a: Yes, as a temporary workaround via USB.

title: No power, no LEDs
shortDescription: Laptop completely unresponsive to power button.
fullDescription: Laptop shows zero signs of life — no LEDs, no fan, no display. Common after a power surge, failed adapter, or motherboard short.

fixSteps.title: Test adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter or known-good Dell adapter to verify power delivery.

fixSteps.title: Drain residual power
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect AC, hold power button 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect battery
fixSteps.instruction: Open laptop, unplug internal battery, try AC only.

whenToCallPro: If component swaps don't restore power.
videoSearchQuery: Dell laptop no power dead fix

faq.q: Could it be the power button?
faq.a: Rarely, but possible on older Inspiron.
